title: How are the mighty fallen (2 Samuel 1:17–27)
hook: David's lament for Saul and Jonathan

segments.voice: Yesterday the medium at Endor set bread before a king with no strength left. Your line was she fed him. Today, news from the battle reaches David.

Two objects are set down in front of David: a crown, and the band from a king's arm. The young man who brings them has come three days from the battle. Saul has fallen on Mount Gilboa, and Jonathan with him. On paper, this is good news for David. The man who threw spears at him and chased him through caves and deserts is gone, and the road to the throne is open. And David tears his clothes. He and his men mourn and weep and fast until evening. Then David does something more. He makes a song.
screen: `SAUL AND JONATHAN, DEAD ON GILBOA.` → `THE ROAD TO THE THRONE IS OPEN.` → `DAVID TEARS HIS CLOTHES.`

segments.voice: The text says David lamented over Saul and over Jonathan, and that the lament is written in the Book of Jashar. It opens with the beauty of Israel slain on the heights, and then the line it keeps coming back to: "How are the mighty fallen!" It isn't a statement. It's a cry, as if the mind can't make it fit. Tell it not in Gath, he says, don't announce it in the streets of Ashkelon, the Philistine cities, so their daughters won't rejoice. He curses the hills of Gilboa: no dew, no rain. Then the hardest part. He praises Saul. Saul and Jonathan, lovely and pleasant in their lives, not divided even in death, swifter than eagles, stronger than lions. Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who dressed you in scarlet and put gold on your clothing. Not a word about the spear or the cave. David doesn't pretend Saul was good to him. He chooses, for the length of a song, to grieve the king and not the enemy. Then the song narrows to one person: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; your love to me was wonderful. The refrain comes back once more at the end: how are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished. Some people are easy to grieve, and some aren't. This song holds both, the friend and the man who hunted him, and gives each of them honest tears.
screen: `WRITTEN IN THE BOOK OF JASHAR.` · `TELL IT NOT IN GATH.` · `WEEP OVER SAUL.` · then, large: `HOW ARE THE MIGHTY FALLEN.` · then: `MY BROTHER JONATHAN.`

segments.voice: Let someone come to mind who is gone, or gone from your life, and who was hard to love. You don't need to forgive or excuse anything; just look for one true thing worth mourning, something they gave, a way they were strong, and let it be sad and mixed at once. If you pray, you can hold David's cry: how are the mighty fallen.
lament. David's song over Saul and Jonathan, grieving the friend and the man who hunted him in the same breath. Today's word.

howItsDone: Jews read David's lament in the book of Samuel, part of the Prophets; the refrain how are the mighty fallen comes three times in the song, in verses 19, 25 and 27.
